name: Question 13
worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{4x} & ⇒ & v=\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{{e}^{4x}}{4}-\int (\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4})\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1/4}x{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & ={\frac{1}{4}x{e}^{4x}|}_{0}^{1/4}-\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{0}^{1/4}{e}^{4x}\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{1}{4}x{e}^{4x}|}_{0}^{1/4}-{\frac{1}{16}{e}^{4x}|}_{0}^{1/4} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\frac{1}{4}{e}^{4(1/4)}-0\cdot {e}^{4\cdot 0}]-\frac{1}{16}[{e}^{4(1/4)}-{e}^{4\cdot 0}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\frac{e}{4}-0]-\frac{1}{16}[e-1] \\  & =\frac{e}{16}-\frac{e}{16}+\frac{1}{16} \\  & =\frac{1}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Let's use integration by parts. We set u=x⇒u′=1v′=e4x⇒v=e4x4.

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫x⋅e4xdx=x⋅e4x4−∫(e4x4)⋅1dx.

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get ∫01/4xe4xdx=14xe4x|01/4−14∫01/4e4xdx=14xe4x|01/4−116e4x|01/4=14[14e4(1/4)−0⋅e4⋅0]−116[e4(1/4)−e4⋅0]=14[e4−0]−116[e−1]=e16−e16+116=116.
